messages:
sophia: Quick follow-up from the kernel selection RFC — need clarity on SM capability gating across A100/H100/L4. TL;DR: can we avoid runtime JIT probing on startup for cold VMs?

ben: Short answer: not entirely. L4 lacks some tensor core ops we rely on; we need a cheap runtime probe (microkernel check) but we can cache result per node.

rahul: Adding details: probe should be a single device query + tiny kernel that checks mma and wmma availability + instruction-set checks. Takes <50ms. Keep in device-level cache keyed by PCI id.

olivia: Ops question: how do we handle live rollouts where we change default kernel order? risk of perf cliffs.

ben: Plan: config with priority list + soft fallback. Example policies:
```
policy:
  - name: prefer_fast_tiled
    devices: [h100, a100]
    kernels: [mma_tiled_v2, fprop_fused]
  - name: fallback_scalar
    devices: [l4]
    kernels: [scalar_attn, kv_caching]
```
We ship policy v1 and can change ordering via config push.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for infra-kernel-policy on 5 nodes in us-west1 tomorrow 03:00 UTC :rocket:

sophia: For cost/latency decisions we need per-kernel P95 and token/s metrics. Proposal: augment telemetry with labels {kernel, device_family, seq_len_bucket}.

rahul: Agreed. Also add counters for kernel-compile-time, fallback_count, and probe_latency.

olivia: Testing matrix idea: microbench across seq lengths [32,128,512,2048] and batch sizes [1,4,16] on each hw family. Compare A100 vs H100 vs L4 for these kernels.

ben: Edge-case: H100 L2 schedulers cause variable throughput in long sequences; we should have runtime heuristic: if seq_len > 1024 and tokens/sec drops >20% then switch to alternative kernel (hot fallback) for that session.

sophia: Sounds good. Who owns the runtime changes + probe lib?

ben: I'll own runtime gating code. rahul owns probe implementation + telemetry. olivia + infra team handle rollout and canary.

sophia: Action items:
- ben: draft PR for policy config + runtime switch (due Tue)
- rahul: probe microkernel + telemetry labels (due Tue)
- olivia: testing matrix and canary plan (due Wed)

olivia: noted. I'll post test harness results in #eng-runtime when ready.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on 5 nodes in us-west1 :white_check_mark:

ben: quick Q: do we allow per-customer pinning to force a kernel? (enterprise use-case)

rahul: yes, add an override field in config: kernel_pin: <kernel_name> that bypasses policy.

sophia: Great. Let's keep kernel names stable (semver). We'll document in runtime API and console controls.

olivia: minor: ensure FSM for session-level switch has a cooldown (e.g., 30s) to avoid flip-flop.

ben: will add cooldown and metric for flip-flops.

sophia: thanks all. filing follow-up RFC note and linking this thread. :sparkles:
